clue.text: Family name of Swiss banker taken in by scam

indicators.note: something taken in by another is held within it, so the banker sits inside the scam

parts.note: a con is a swindle or scam
the gnomes of Zurich is a mocking name for Swiss bankers

explanation.surface: A Swiss financier is caught up in a fraud, with a family name thrown in for detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gnomes of Zurich' is an old British jibe at Swiss bankers; 'taken in by' signals the enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: A cognomen was the third, inherited name of a Roman citizen, hence a surname or family name.

clue.text: Lizard in S American region, one moving to prime position

indicators.note: the prime position in a word is its front, so this letter is shifted to the start

parts.note: Guiana is the region on the north-east coast of South America
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A lizard lives in a South American region, and one creature jostles to the front.
explanation.walkthrough: In GUIANA, the I moves to the front, giving IGUANA.
explanation.definitionFit: The iguana is a large tropical American lizard, so it is an example of the reptile group named.

clue.text: Achieve prominent publicity making banners?

definitions.meaning: banner headlines run across a front page, so making them is literally hitting the headlines; the question mark flags the play

explanation.surface: Someone gets famous by producing big printed banners.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be reported prominently in the press, and a banner is the largest kind of newspaper headline.

clue.text: Illustrious celebrity entertaining the Spanish Left

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to have them in, so the celebrity holds the other letters

parts.note: a star is a celebrity
el is the Spanish for 'the'

explanation.surface: A famous star plays host to the Spanish Left, a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' signals that the celebrity holds the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Stellar means starry, and figuratively outstanding or brilliant, much like illustrious.

clue.text: Affair of big cat crossing road with last of cubs

indicators.note: the cat lies across the other letters, spanning them on either side

parts.note: a lion is a big cat
the A1 is Britain's longest numbered road, here written AI with the digit as I

indicators.note: picks the final letter of the word cubs

explanation.surface: A lioness affair: the big cat crosses a road with the last of her cubs.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is the main road from London to Edinburgh; read with 1 as the letter I. 'crossing' signals the enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is a sexual or romantic relationship, especially a secret one, so an affair.

clue.text: Confusion brought about by inspector's instruction

parts.note: DI is Detective Inspector, so DI's is the inspector's
an order is an instruction

explanation.surface: Chaos follows a detective inspector's command.
explanation.walkthrough: DI is a British police rank, Detective Inspector.
explanation.definitionFit: Disorder is a lack of order, a state of confusion or muddle.

clue.text: Liberal leaving place of worship in wooded vale

indicators.note: the Liberal departs, so that letter is taken out of the building

parts.note: a temple is a place of worship
L is the abbreviation for Liberal, the British party

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician walks out of a temple into a leafy valley.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vale of Tempe is a famous wooded gorge in Thessaly, Greece, and its name became poetic for any lovely valley.

clue.text: Wizardry of fighting man in rainproof garment

indicators.note: one piece sits within the other, the soldier wearing the coat

parts.note: a mac, short for mackintosh, is a raincoat
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier in a raincoat performs some wizardry.
explanation.definitionFit: Magic is sorcery or the art of the wizard, and figuratively any amazing skill.

clue.text: Neatly trim thick hair covering current dog

indicators.note: the hair goes over and around the other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: a mane is a thick head of hair
I is the symbol for electric current
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A dog groomer trims a mutt's thick coat neatly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' signals the hair enclosing the rest; I is the physics symbol for electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: To manicure is to tend the nails, and by extension to clip or tidy anything carefully, such as a lawn.

clue.text: Taking notice of ambassador, say, limiting noise

parts.note: HE is His (or Her) Excellency, an ambassador's title

indicators.note: to limit is to bound on both sides, so these letters hold the noise between them

parts.note: eg, for example, is what 'say' means in 'a fruit, say'
din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: Someone listens to an ambassador who is perhaps keeping the noise down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like a link word but supplies the abbreviation for 'for example'; 'limiting' signals that it encloses the noise.
explanation.definitionFit: To heed is to pay attention to, so heeding is paying attention to something or someone.

clue.text: Gibbon, for one, a senior cleric

definitions.meaning: an archbishop or the chief bishop of a country

explanation.surface: Gibbon, perhaps the historian, is cast as a senior churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: Gibbon looks like Edward Gibbon the historian; it is the ape.
explanation.definitionFit: Primates are the order of apes and monkeys, and primate is also the title of a leading archbishop.

clue.text: Great hopes Berg cultivated about a stage work

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go round the single letter, enclosing it
cultivated ground is worked over, so these letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: The composer Berg nurtures great hopes for a theatrical piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cultivated' rearranges GREATHOPESBERG, and 'about' puts that round A. Alban Berg was an opera composer, a fitting decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: John Gay's 1728 ballad opera satirising high society is a famous work for the theatre.

clue.text: Money you and I brought back for evergreen tree

parts.note: cash is money

indicators.note: bringing something back returns it the other way, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: we means you and I

explanation.surface: We bring cash home to spend on a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The cashew is a tropical American evergreen whose kidney-shaped nut is widely eaten.

clue.text: Cheek of learner leaving lucky creature outside hotel

indicators.note: the shortened creature wraps round the outside of the hotel letter
the learner goes, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: in Britain a black cat crossing your path is thought lucky
L is the learner driver's plate
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A learner's cheeky talk drives a lucky cat from outside a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes L from BLACKCAT to give BACKCAT, and 'outside' wraps that round H.
explanation.definitionFit: Backchat is cheeky or insolent answering back, a form of impudence.

clue.text: Joint party-giver's charge for keeping house

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so the house letters sit inside the charge

parts.note: a cost is a charge or price

explanation.surface: A co-organiser of a party pays for keeping the house.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after the definition stands for 'is', linking it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A cohost shares hosting duties, so is one of two or more people throwing a party together.

clue.text: Understanding crowd

definitions.meaning: to gather is to infer or understand

explanation.definitionFit: Gathering can mean inferring from evidence and also a group of people who have come together.

clue.text: Eponymous hero's extremely offbeat greeting

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: hello is a greeting

explanation.surface: A title character greets people in an oddball way.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after the definition stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello is the title character of Shakespeare's tragedy, so the play is named after its hero.

clue.text: Woman finally changes sides, finding compound

indicators.note: the last letter is a side, left, and is swapped for the other side, right

parts.note: Ethel is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman finally defects to the other side and finds a chemical.
explanation.walkthrough: The final L (left) of ETHEL changes to R (right).
explanation.definitionFit: Ether, diethyl ether, is an organic chemical compound once used as an anaesthetic.

clue.text: Good worker everyone held to be brave and chivalrous

indicators.note: everyone is held between the other two pieces, enclosed by them

parts.note: the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A good worker is regarded by everyone as brave and noble.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallant describes someone courageous, and also courteous and attentive in the manner of a knight.

clue.text: Woman's name concealed by mature son

indicators.note: the name letter is hidden away inside the other pieces

parts.note: to age is to mature

explanation.surface: A woman keeps her name hidden from her grown-up son.
explanation.definitionFit: Agnes is a woman's given name.

clue.text: No-show sailors put on course right away

parts.note: an AB is an able seaman, so ABS are sailors

indicators.note: the right letter is sent away, removed from the course

parts.note: an entree is a course of a meal

explanation.surface: Sailors are put on a course and promptly fail to turn up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' looks like 'immediately'; it removes R from ENTREE to give ENTEE.
explanation.definitionFit: An absentee is someone expected who does not appear, so a no-show.

clue.text: Witch briefly keeping old Scottish pot for boiling

indicators.note: to keep is to hold, so the shortened witch holds the Scots word inside
a word cut short loses its last letter

parts.note: a crone is an ugly old woman, often a witch
auld is the Scots for old

explanation.surface: A witch keeps an old Scottish pot boiling, as in Macbeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' drops the witch's final letter, and 'keeping' has what remains hold the Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: A cauldron is a large metal pot for boiling over a fire, famously used by witches.

clue.text: US politician eager to crush Yankee rabble-rousing

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting on top of another crushes it, so the Yankee letter comes last

parts.note: Dem is short for a Democrat
agog means eager
Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A US politician eager to crush the Yankees whips up a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Demagogy is the practice of stirring up popular passions to gain power, which is rabble-rousing.

clue.text: African city reached by libertine in thirty-one days

indicators.note: the libertine sits inside the month

parts.note: March is a month of thirty-one days
a rake is a dissolute man

explanation.surface: A playboy arrives in an African city during a month-long trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Marrakech is a major city in Morocco, North Africa.

clue.text: Forceful chap I met at sea

indicators.note: being at sea means confused, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A forceful man is described whom the speaker met on a voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphatic means expressed with force and clarity, so vigorous or forceful.

clue.text: Egyptian citizen displays anger, breaking stick

indicators.note: the anger breaks into the stick, splitting it open

parts.note: a cane is a walking stick
ire is anger

explanation.surface: An angry Egyptian snaps a walking stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cairene is a native or inhabitant of Cairo, the Egyptian capital.

clue.text: Outstanding feature primarily of go-ahead Native American

parts.note: the chin stands out, literally, from the face

indicators.note: primarily picks out the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: an OK is permission, the go-ahead

explanation.surface: A prominent part of a go-getting plan.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chinook are a people of the Pacific Northwest of the United States.

clue.text: Vehicle has got hired to go round old Mediterranean area

indicators.note: the hired letters go round the vehicle, enclosing it

parts.note: let means rented out, hired
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A rental van is taken on a tour of the eastern Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has got' is padding; 'to go round' has the hired word enclose the vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Levant is the old name for the lands of the eastern Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: English archdeacon's betting odds

parts.note: Ven, the Venerable, is an archdeacon's title, so Ven's is the archdeacon's

explanation.surface: An English churchman's bookmaker's odds.
explanation.walkthrough: Archdeacons in the Church of England are styled the Venerable.
explanation.definitionFit: Evens are odds of one to one, where the winnings equal the stake.

clue.text: Weatherproof coat old man wrapped round chest

indicators.note: the old man is wrapped round the chest, enclosing it

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father, the old man
an ark is a chest or box, as in the Ark of the Covenant

explanation.surface: An old man wraps a weatherproof coat around his chest.
explanation.definitionFit: A parka is a hooded windproof jacket, originally an Inuit garment.
